For intricate shapes, discretization via unstructured grids makes direct potential calculation using quadrature prohibitively expensive. This study proposes a straightforward yet efficient high-order scheme for determining these potentials by employing Green's third identity to convert volume integrals into boundary forms that are well-suited for the Helsing-Ojala method. Consequently, the traditionally heavy computation time required for self-interaction and nearfield evaluations on unstructured grids becomes approximately equal to that of farfield interaction calculations handled by the Fast Multipole Method (FMM). A cornerstone of this algorithm is a high-order monomial FMM implementation featuring a novel, simple translation operator. Furthermore, the authors present a hybrid FMM approach to complement the standard version, addressing limitations arising from high oscillatory behavior of translation operator expansions. Together, these methods achieve a total computational complexity of $O(N \log N)$ for domains discretized with $N$ degrees of freedom, while maintaining a simple volume-to-boundary conversion applicable to various shapes.
